utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So good morning, everybody, and good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Let's proceed by calling the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. From the Defence teams I only notice the absence of Mr. Ostojic and Ms. Kondon, yes, and Ms. Kondon. From the Prosecution side I see Mr. McCloskey and Ms. Janisiewicz and no one else. No preliminaries, I take it, so let's go -- there's also -- let's go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: There's no problem with the counsel for the witness to be present.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's a very short matter indeed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No cameras in that direction, please. All right, go ahead, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to express at this point in time that we appreciate the Court's holding at page 10, lines 4 to 7 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- concerning the time which will be used for

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: accused Vinko Padurevic. But, Mr. President, we would like to put on the record - and I speak for this team at least at this point in time - that I am particularly worried about what the Trial Chamber said that we will immediately intervene if there are repetitive questions and we will stop you. Mr. President, we believe that the Trial Chamber has been patient, if not very patient, with my colleague representing the accused Vinko Padurevic, and that we should not be penalised in this respect. I understand that if repetitive questions lead nowhere, then of course I anticipate that I will be stopped when I do my cross-examination. But there are areas that I will go into which indeed will be a repetition of what was done by my colleague, and that was to -- the aim of this will be to elicit different evidence, to speak to the witness with a different angle of approach and with a different aim. And I hope, Mr. President, that the Trial Chamber will be as patient with me as it was with my colleague. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the last thing you can criticise this Trial Chamber for is lack of patience, and -- but you can, of course, and your experience should suffice here, without the need of repeating the questions to elicit the same answer. You can go straight with the witness straight to the part where he supposedly has stated, et cetera, say, This is your statement, now I have got some questions for you. This is basically the way you should go about, in other words. Of course you can revisit certain areas if you're not happy with the testimony of the witness. But there are ways and means of doing it. You don't go through the whole process of asking the same questions again, only to find out that he is giving the same answers. Go straight to -- this is -- go straight to the point. This is what we have -- and then of course we'll use our discretion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will endeavour to do so and I appreciate the Court's holding. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Zivanovic, if we are going to continue on this, I think we better go --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to join the submission of Mr. Bourgon. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would also join that, because obviously we have different interests with different accused, as you well know, and you have been very patient with us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's now go back to closed session. Get the witness back in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 22nd day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
